Literally, it was the worst experience of my life.
I have been a member of Elite Luxury Spa for over 2 years but I have been to Malad outlet only twice because of the kind of therapists they have and the kind of customer service that they give.

I had an appointment at their Kandivali outlet today but due to some reason I couldn’t make it.
I decided to go to Malad instead as I had sprained my ankle and had a terrible back pain, thinking that it would help to get a massage.
I told them about all my requirements and needs, they agreed and said will convey it to the therapist and give me the best one that is available.
The therapist, Ms. Mary, didn’t know anything as she walked in.
Was lost the entire time. It just felt like she was pouring oil over me and was just rubbing. Didn’t even feel a little like massage where you kind of feel some pressure.
And when I asked her to remove the knots in my back, rather than massaging it over and working her way through it, she pressed over the knot so hard that it hurt me even more.
More so, she was yawning every 5 mins, using wrong techniques and also using only one hand to the massage.
After all of this, once she completed, she forgot to switch on the steam due to which I had to wait for about 10 mins to get steam and then take a shower and leave.
What is more disappointing is that, the receptionist rather than asking me about my experience or apologising to me for the error made by the therapist, she is saying ‘If I would have known that you would take this long, I would have refunded your money and asked you to leave’.
I mean, are you serious?

I understand that it is your closing time and everything but 10 mins hardly makes a difference especially when you want to retain a customer.

The arrogance that staff have at this particular location is beyond comprehension.
I feel that I wasted my hours here today because the therapy was terrible and the customer service even worse.

The therapist was skilled and the massage technique was effective—helped ease muscle tension and felt professionally delivered.

However, the overall environment fell short of expectations. The headrest pillow was too firm, causing neck strain while lying face down. Water was leaking from the A/C in my room, and there was a faint squeaking noise from outside or a neighboring room, which disrupted the ambience. Decent for the massage quality, but the space needs improvement to justify the price and deliver a more rejuvenating experience.

I went in yesterday for massage at Bodhi Thai Spa, Malad and took service of 3750 rupees. I have been visiting this place for more than 4 years now and this is the first time it so happened that my money was stolen from my wallet. It was my bad that before leaving for home I did not check my wallet as it did not occur to me that my money might have been stolen.

I came back home and later that evening I went out to purchase few things and when I reached my wallet I realised my money isn’t there. My entire cash of 1700 rupees was missing.

When today, I called up the receptionist she told me none of their therapist have such habit and they might have not done this. But my question to the owner is why would I lie about my money stolen when I am regular customer and have been taking on an average 3000 rupees of services every time I visit.

Ofcourse this is a tricky situation which I understand. But this is really very disappointing to know that customers money is stolen and there is no apology either nor any kind of investigation. When I asked to question the therapist who gave me massage, receptionist said she is on weekly off today.

I don’t understand how should I ever trust Bodhi Thai Spa, Malad location with my valuables. Please don’t say that you shouldn’t bring in money and stuff. It is not my fault that I carry money in my wallet for emergencies.

This is really disappointing and I would never visit this location ever for any services now.

featured_reviews.name: Quirky Wanderer
featured_reviews.review_text:
While aromatherapy and Balinese massages are quite common in Mumbai, the newly opened Bamboo spa has a few unheard treatments like an actual Bamboo massage with heated bamboo bamboo sticks and signature healing therapies like a Tibetan Ku Nye massage and Manipura massage.

I decided to go with the Tibetan Ku Nye massage and here’s my review: it’s an ancient therapeutic healing massage, Ku means applying oil and Nye means kneading.
A medium pressure massage where they massage the acupressure points with oils  like rose, lavender, lemongrass and Tulsi, followed by the use of Potli with Tibetan music playing in the background. The goal is to enhance the energy flow in the body and calm down the nervous system. Exactly what my stressed body needed. Post massage you have an option of green tea or buckwheat tea. Go for the latter :)
My therapist Gloria was amazing and this was Hands down one of the best spa therapies I have had in Mumbai. My body went into a snooze mode post this for hours. It was so relaxing and calming.
Absolutely recommend! 10/10!
